findings.title: Recurring-event calendar deletions are never awaited and may never start
findings.body: In the recurring-event cancellation branch, the code does `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. Because `getCalendar` is now async (dynamic import), the entire body of the forEach callback — including the very first `calendar.deleteEvent(...)` call — is deferred until after the dynamic import resolves. Previously `getCalendar` was synchronous, so the first `deleteEvent` was at least initiated synchronously inside the callback. The handler later does `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) using the contents of `apiDeletes` at that moment, which is still empty/partial because the async callbacks haven't run yet, and then returns the response. On serverless platforms the function can be frozen once the response is sent, so the external calendar events for all remaining recurring booking instances may never be deleted, leaving stale events on users' calendars. The pushed values are also the awaited results rather than promises, so they were never going to be awaited anyway. Use `await Promise.all(credentials.map(async ...))` and push the actual promises before awaiting.

findings.title: requestReschedule deletes calendar/video events fire-and-forget via async forEach
findings.body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` launches async work that nothing awaits. Before this PR `getCalendar` was synchronous, so `deleteEvent` was at least invoked synchronously inside the forEach; now the await on the dynamic import defers even the initiation of the deletion past the end of the mutation, and the mutation returns its response without waiting. In a serverless environment the deletions can be dropped entirely, leaving cancelled events on attendees' calendars, and any rejection (import failure, deleteEvent failure) becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being logged. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` (with individual `.catch` for logging) before sending the reschedule email/returning.

findings.title: Calendar/video deletions run un-awaited inside async forEach; surrounding try/catch is now dead
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` fires off async callbacks that nothing awaits, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return immediately. Previously `getCalendar` was synchronous so `deleteEvent` was at least initiated synchronously; with the new `await getCalendar(...)` the deletion isn't even started until the dynamic import resolves, which races with the function returning (risky in serverless, where the process can freeze after the response). Additionally, errors thrown inside these async callbacks — including dynamic-import failures — reject outside the surrounding try/catch (lines 124–139), producing unhandled rejections rather than the logged errors the catch block intends. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` inside the try block.

findings.title: Calendar/video deletions run un-awaited inside async forEach; surrounding try/catch is now dead
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` fires off async callbacks that nothing awaits, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return immediately. Previously `getCalendar` was synchronous so `deleteEvent` was at least initiated synchronously; with the new `await getCalendar(...)` the deletion isn't even started until the dynamic import resolves, which races with the function returning (risky in serverless, where the process can freeze after the response). Additionally, errors thrown inside these async callbacks — including dynamic-import failures — reject outside the surrounding try/catch (lines 124–139), producing unhandled rejections rather than the logged errors the catch block intends. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` inside the try block.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly at module load, so nothing is actually lazy-loaded
findings.body: Each entry like `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` is evaluated when the `@calcom/app-store` module itself is first imported, which immediately kicks off loading of every app's chunk. Because the import() expressions run at object-literal evaluation time (not on property access), importing this module anywhere starts fetching all ~28 app bundles at once — there is no per-app deferral, only code splitting. If the intent of the PR is to defer loading apps until they are used, the values need to be lazy thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) with call sites adjusted. As written, the change also converts app-module load failures into rejected promises stored in this object, which will surface as unhandled rejections for any app that is never explicitly awaited.
